bibliographic.title: Unmasking the Shadows of AI: Investigating Deceptive Capabilities in Large Language Models
bibliographic.citation_apa: Guo, L. (2023). Unmasking the shadows of AI: Investigating deceptive capabilities in large language models. University College London.

methodology.method_family: narrative essay with literature review and evaluative commentary
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models (LLMs), ChatGPT (GPT), chatbots, search engines

eligibility.decision_rationale: The text is a conceptual essay on deceptive behaviors in LLMs, AI Safety Summit 2023, and high-level international governance, with only peripheral mention of chatbots and no operational treatment of conversational governance, guardrails, observability, audit, human oversight, or regulated deployment controls central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial front-matter pages were supplied; bibliographic metadata uses a placeholder title and venue is not stated in the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Self-described essay combining literature review, categorization of deception types, and evaluative commentary; author acknowledges literature is predominantly from arXiv and deficient in social science contribution. No empirical sampling, data collection protocol, or systematic review method is described in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is internally coherent on LLM deception and macro-governance discourse, but evidence adequacy is limited by reliance on secondary and arXiv-heavy sources without a transparent search strategy; relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is indirect.

coding.theme: Deceptive capabilities and governance discourse in LLMs
coding.subtheme: Categorization of deception types and AI Safety Summit evaluation
rq_alignment: risk and harm in generative AI

synthesis.main_claim: Deceptive behavior in LLMs is an inherent phenomenon tied to model advancement and biases, categorized as strategic deception, imitation, sycophancy, and unfaithful reasoning, with significant social risks requiring international governance and educational responses.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a conceptual taxonomy of LLM deception and a critical evaluation of the AI Safety Summit 2023 alongside discussion of biases, chatbot use contexts, and high-level governance considerations.
synthesis.limitations: Predominantly arXiv-based literature with limited social science contribution; essay format without described systematic evidence synthesis; partial text prevents assessment of full argument and methods.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on LLM deception, bias, and macro-governance discourse; not suitable as central evidence for operational conversational governance, guardrails, observability, audit, or regulated deployment controls.

evidence.claim: Study focuses on deceptive behaviors of LLMs via conceptual essay and literature review
evidence.excerpt: This research critically navigates the intricate landscape of AI deception, concentrating on deceptive behaviours of Large Language Models (LLMs).
